exercise.name: Dumbbell Full Swing

reference.title: Dumbbell Full Swing
reference.listing: Video; the page could not be read here (blocked), so the movement follows the name and standard coaching (two-hand swing finishing overhead).
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (explosive hip extension from a hinge; the arms carry the dumbbell overhead)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in on the way down, a sharp breath out as the hips snap; breathe in again as the dumbbell falls.

prescription.load: User-chosen; lighter than for a chest-height swing, because it has to be controlled overhead
prescription.progression: Master the chest-height (Russian) swing first; then go higher, then heavier

cues.text: Feet wider than the hips, toes slightly out; one dumbbell held vertically by the handle in both hands.
Hinge: hips back, flat back, dumbbell between the thighs.
Snap the hips and keep the arms long; let the dumbbell float all the way overhead, arms by the ears.
Let it fall straight back down in front; hinge late and hike it through.
Snap again: glutes tight, ribs down; do not arch to get it overhead.
Let the dumbbell slow down and stop hanging in front.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the lower back to reach overhead
mistakes.fix: Ribs down and glutes tight; stop at chest height if the shoulders cannot reach overhead with a neutral back.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the dumbbell with the arms
mistakes.fix: The hip snap moves it; the arms only guide.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the dumbbell drift behind the head at the top
mistakes.fix: Finish with the dumbbell straight over the shoulders and the arms by the ears.

kinematics.setup: ≈93° at the bottom (joint channel), trunk ≈47° forward
kinematics.norm: Kettlebell swing: about 75 degrees of hip flexion at the start to about 1 degree of extension at the top (McGill 2012)
About 69 degrees at the bottom to about 2 degrees of extension at the top in the kettlebell swing (McGill 2012); a hinge, not a squat

kinematics.setup: Arms 20° behind vertical, dumbbell between the thighs
kinematics.peak: Arms ≈161° from hanging (overhead, by the ears), shoulder elevation 168°
kinematics.norm: Full (American) swing: the arms finish overhead with the load straight over the shoulders (standard coaching; clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: About 1.9 s per swing (0.9 s up, 1 s down), two swings, then park
kinematics.norm: Fast contraction-relaxation cycles over about half a second in the swing (McGill 2012); about 2 s per overhead swing (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #7582, Dumbbell Full Swing, video (movement reference)
McGill & Marshall 2012, kettlebell swing, snatch, and bottoms-up carry: back and hip muscle activation, motion, and low back loads (J Strength Cond Res 26(1):16-27)

cautions: Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Shoulder pain, instability or limited overhead mobility: swing only to chest height.
Low-back pain: keep the back flat; stop the set when the hips slow down or the back rounds.
Hold the handle firmly; clear the space in front of and above you.
Load is user-chosen: start light, the overhead finish multiplies the shoulder demand.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Drives the explosive hip extension that carries the dumbbell up; glute activity in the kettlebell swing was high in McGill 2012.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Drives the explosive hip extension that carries the dumbbell up; glute activity in the kettlebell swing was high in McGill 2012.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Load in the hinge and help snap the hips through; lengthened at the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Load in the hinge and help snap the hips through; lengthened at the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the back flat in the hinge; McGill 2012 measured high back-extensor activity in the swing.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the back flat in the hinge; McGill 2012 measured high back-extensor activity in the swing.
muscleNotes.quads_r: Extend the knees at the top (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Extend the knees at the top (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Guides the straight arms up the last part of the arc to overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Guides the straight arms up the last part of the arc to overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Helps hold the arms overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Helps hold the arms overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Stops the ribs flaring and the back arching at the top (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blades up for the overhead finish (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Rotates the shoulder blades up for the overhead finish (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Supports the shoulder girdle overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Supports the shoulder girdle overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the falling dumbbell back down and through the legs (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the falling dumbbell back down and through the legs (clinical opinion).
